policies.policy_name: Mandatory Field Presence for SLA Update
policies.description: When calling the update_sla_definition tool, the mandatory field sla_def_id must be supplied. The request must be rejected if this field is missing.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: The update_sla_definition call must be the only operation performed in a request; no additional actions may be combined with it.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.policy_name: Record State Validation Before SLA Update
policies.description: The update_sla_definition operation may proceed only if the current SLA definition record is in a state that permits updates (e.g., not locked or in the middle of another transaction).
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: When updating an SLA definition, only the allowed fields (e.g., target_mins, active, pause_on_pending, applies_to_priority, schedule, name, metric) may be modified. Attempts to add or change unsupported metric fields must be rejected.

Updates to an SLA definition must not disable the required pausing of the SLA timer when an incident is on hold for the enumerated reasons. The pause_on_pending flag may be changed, but the system must still enforce pausing under the defined conditions.
references: SLA Pause: The SLA timer must be paused (stage = paused) when the Incident is in stage = on_hold and the on_hold_reason is one of the following enumerations: Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.

policies.description: Any change to an SLA definition (e.g., active or target_mins) must preserve the breach‑handling behavior: if an SLA exceeds its duration, the incident’s escalation flag must be set to true and a notification sent to the Manager.
references: Breach: If the SLA exceeds its duration (stage = breached), the escalation flag on the Incident must be set to true, and an automatic notification sent to the Manager.

policies.policy_name: Role‑Based Access for SLA Definition Updates
policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role are authorized to invoke update_sla_definition. Users with Manager, Agent, or Reporter roles must be denied.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.

policies.description: If the caller’s role does not have permission to perform update_sla_definition, the assistant must halt the operation and return a 403 Forbidden error.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: When the update_sla_definition endpoint returns a rate‑limit error, the assistant must pause and retry using an exponential backoff strategy rather than retrying immediately.
references: Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policies.description: Before invoking update_sla_definition, the assistant must verify that the provided sla_def_id corresponds to an existing SLA definition record. The operation must not proceed if the identifier cannot be resolved, and an appropriate error indicating “SLA definition not found” must be returned.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.policy_name: Record Conflict Handling (409 Conflict) for SLA Updates
policies.description: If the SLA definition record is locked, being modified by another process, or otherwise in a state that prevents the update, the assistant must halt the operation and return a 409 Conflict error. No changes may be applied when such a conflict is detected.
references: 409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.
